data.title: Lebanon becomes first Middle East country to end death penalty
data.description: Lebanon’s parliament voted on Tuesday to abolish the death penalty, making the country the first in the Middle East to do so. Lebanon has not carried out an execution since 2004, but death sentences have continued to be handed down, with the latest issued on Monday. Amnesty International says at least 85 people were still on death row as of January this year. Capital punishment in Lebanon has typically applied to serious crimes including murder, terrorism and espionage. France 24 correspondent Renée Davis reports the latest from Beirut.

data.title: Faced with ageing population, Vietnam seeks to curb falling birthrate
data.description: Vietnam, a country of more than 100 million people, is facing a sharp decline in its birthrate. Once known for large families, the nation's fertility rate has fallen to just 1.9 children per woman. This figure worries the government, which for decades was obsessed with controlling population growth. For more than 40 years, a two-child policy was the norm in Vietnam – a restriction that was only lifted in June 2025.

data.title: A bungled bomb plot in Poland exposed a spy – but whose spy was he?
data.description: When exiled Russian opposition campaigner Igor Rogov was accused of working for the Kremlin, his friends were shocked. Could this young activist have really been an undercover agent? • The summer issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to order The police came for Igor Rogov because someone had mailed him a bomb-making kit. The eclectic mix of items – a chrome vacuum flask, a pair of marker pens, a power bank and a bottle of antifreeze fluid – might have seemed innocuous to an untrained eye, but Poland was on high alert in July 2024. Two months previously, a shopping mall in Warsaw had burned down in an arson attack; an Ikea in neighbouring Lithuania was also set on fire . Authorities believed it was a sabotage campaign masterminded by Russia’s intelligence services, intended to sow panic and undermine support for Ukraine. They feared it was only a matter of time before the Kremlin escalated further. A security officer at the parcel company’s warehouse was suspicious enough about the package to call in the authorities, who arrived with sniffer dogs and special equipment. X-rays of the marker pens showed they had 1980s Soviet-produced detonators concealed inside, while the flask had a false bottom containing a sachet of metallic powder. The power bank appeared to have been tampered with in some way, and a probe of the bottled liquid showed it contained a highly volatile nitroglycerine solution. With the right expertise, the items could be turned into a powerful bomb. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I ran away to Paris to be a writer and ended up begging’: Bill Nighy on dashed dreams, golf emojis and playing a cranky novelist
data.description: As his new film & Sons hits the screen, the actor turned podcast agony uncle relives his ‘cliched’ ambitions, deplores working lunches – and yearns to do the splits like Prince A dying patriarch summons his brood for a dramatic announcement. It may not be the most original starting point for a movie, but & Sons adds an eccentric twist – one that it would be unfair to reveal here but which nudges the material into the realm of science fiction. The father in question is a revered novelist who is as reclusive as JD Salinger and as whiskery and dishevelled as Catweazle. Dormant for decades, the fictional AN Dyer is first glimpsed in a horizontal position on the sofa, refusing to come to the telephone: “I don’t do phonecalls,” he grumbles. That is patently not true of the actor who plays him. “I spend a lot of time on the phone,” Bill Nighy says breezily. He is speaking to me from north-west London, where he has been nosing around bookshops. “I’m also an enthusiastic texter. I was always very quick on the old Nokia. Quite proud of myself, I was.” Where does he stand on emojis? “I used to be philosophically opposed. Most of them are a bit naff.” He then proceeds to list the exceptions. “I like the flamingo and the purple dahlia. I like the leaping shark. Sometimes I combine it with the leaping dolphin. Very occasionally, I like the golfer in mid-swing if I’m congratulating someone. I don’t do smiley faces.” Continue reading...

data.title: I got married in the Vegas of Europe. It was the most romantic 20 minutes of my life | Jules Darmanin
data.description: Post-Brexit visa rules and faceless pen-pushers were keeping me and my partner apart. But love finds a way Consider your ideal wedding. You may picture religious pageantry, majestic domes and the auspicious light of the Divine beaming on a white dress. Maybe you see friends dancing on a pub’s veranda, cheering for you in front of a town hall, or anywhere really – the people you love are there, and it’s all that matters. What you are probably not picturing is a meet-up with Chris and Mitch, two complete strangers waiting for you and your future spouse by a nondescript fountain in the middle of Copenhagen. Judging by my soon-to-be-wife’s bewildered laugh throughout the entire 20 minutes of our wedding, this is not what she was picturing either. data.title: ‘I’ve been on plenty of dates – but nothing happened’: are we looking at the death of the kiss?
data.description: Call it a crisis, call it a decline, call it a recession: the long, lusty snog is in trouble, harder to experience in real life or even watch on screen. But why? And what’s it like to think you may never lock lips with another? Spencer’s last kiss was two years ago, on a first date. It started off promisingly: after matching on Tinder, they met for a walk, then got drinks and ice-cream, before having dinner at her place. Finally, they kissed. “I didn’t like it,” says Spencer. He still struggles to identify why. “I found her attractive. There was chemistry, but something was lacking. There was nothing behind the kiss – it felt like a mechanical thing to do.” That wasn’t just Spencer’s most recent kiss – it was his first ever, at the age of 29. Now 31, he says a second kiss in some ways feels less possible than having sex: “The jump feels way bigger.” Continue reading...

data.title: An Amputation Obsession: the Monster and the Surgeon review – an engrossing story, if you can stomach it
data.description: This documentary follows the shocking case of Neil Hopper, a top surgeon who had his own legs removed due to a fetish. No fetish or obsession is unique, and the internet can always connect you with others whose minds work the same way. It’s one of the great blessings and curses of the digital age, and central to An Amputation Obsession: the Monster and the Surgeon, a two-part documentary on which the “contains material some viewers may find disturbing” disclaimer is no exaggeration. We begin at the Royal Cornwall hospital, known locally as Treliske, in Truro, Cornwall. It used to have a man on its staff who was a minor medical superstar: Neil Hopper, a vascular surgeon, was well known for his clinical expertise and comforting bedside manner, particularly when advising on and performing amputations. He acquired full hero status in 2019, when he was diagnosed with sepsis and had both legs amputated below the knee but miraculously returned to work within six months, astonishing physiotherapists and other medical professionals with how well he adapted to disability. An Amputation Obsession: the Monster and the Surgeon is on Prime Video Continue reading...

data.title: Mrs Stern Wanders the Prussian State Library review – interrogating Hannah Arendt
data.description: Traverse theatre, Edinburgh An encounter in a police cell with a Nazi officer could have been the end of the political theorist, but Jenny Lyn Bader’s play has little feel for the dramatic The Mrs Stern of the title is the married name of Hannah Arendt , the political theorist much remembered for her “banality of evil” insight. Jenny Lyn Bader sets her play not, as you might expect, in the Prussian state library, but in a police cell where Arendt has been hauled in for questioning not long after the Reichstag fire. The Nazi apparatus has extended its remit to political crimes and she, what with her bookish ways, errant husband and associations with Jewish intellectuals, has come under scrutiny. data.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for figs with raspberry cream and cat tongue biscuits | A kitchen in Rome
data.description: Combine these simple Italian baked treats with chilled fruit and thick cream for a playful summer pudding In his exquisite The French Menu Cookbook , Richard Olney has clear ideas and strong opinions about everything, including dessert. He believed that rich desserts should follow only the simplest of meals, whereas with most menus (meaning all the sophisticated menus in his book), something light, airy and playful is best. His suggestions read like a summer fruit poem: peach melba, apple mousse with peaches, apricot fritters dusted with icing sugar, strawberries in sweetened orange juice, strawberries in beaujolais, strawberry mousse with raspberry puree, iced cherries and fresh almonds. One of his late summer/early autumn menus also suggests fresh figs with raspberry cream ( figues à la crème framboise ), which is both fun to make (the red puree streaking through the cream for a raspberry ripple) and to eat. An airy and playful pudding calls for an airy and playful biscuit. What better than lingue di gatto, or cat tongues, so called because of their flat, elongated shape. Made from butter, sugar, flour, and egg whites, lingue di gatto are not complicated to make, but do require a piping bag, which can be mimicked by a zip-lock bag – just remember to scrape the mixture into the bag first, and only snip the end off when you are ready to pipe. Continue reading...

data.title: The Spy Next Door review – a wild story … once the endless string of men have stopped talking
data.description: The gripping case of Russian spy Anna Chapman somehow becomes quite dull in parts of this very male documentary. Thank goodness for the only woman to speak in it  – who livens things up ahead of a thrilling ending In June 2010, Anna Chapman was arrested in New York City as part of a major FBI operation targeting Russian spies. Members of the “illegals programme” had, for decades, ingratiated themselves into American workplaces and communities, all while working for Russia’s foreign intelligence service (SVR). While Chapman was ostensibly in the US to sell real estate to wealthy Russians, she was something of an outlier among the group. The 28-year-old had been in Manhattan for only a year, having spent much of the previous decade in London. There, she had married (and later separated from) a British citizen, Alex Chapman. It was also where she may or may not have been initially recruited as a Russian state asset. Her connections to Britain would, for a while, make Anna Chapman a tabloid mainstay; here we see her ex, Marcus Read, reading an old interview he did with the Mirror, headlined “My crazy six weeks of passion with Russian spy girl Anna Chapman”. The working title of this two-part documentary was Red Hot Spy: The Anna Chapman Story. Indeed, much is made of how irresistibly alluring and apparently manipulative Chapman was, and the pull of her flame-coloured locks (tabloid infamy also coincided with a dye job). Read met Chapman in Zimbabwe, and she ended up joining him in Brighton for a time, before ditching him at a techno night to embark on a relationship with Alex Chapman. “Here I am, 20-odd years later ,still talking about it,” says Read, perhaps wistful, clearly still incredulous. It is, maybe, the first clue that The Spy Next Door doesn’t contain any big new revelations about Chapman (who has returned to Russia and didn’t want to be involved with the programme), but rather is a slick reworking of old news. The Spy Next Door: The Anna Chapman Story is on Channel 4 Continue reading...

data.title: Jason Arday is now the stick the right will use to beat back racial equality. Don’t let that happen | Afua Hirsch
data.description: The UK is far from equality in academia or society. You don’t need a Cambridge degree to see that Arday’s story is being used to stop any progress in its tracks In 1987, a college at the University of Cambridge considered offering a prestigious position to a black man in what would be the first appointment of its kind. Not only did the man not have a degree, but he had left school at the age of 13, struggling with dyslexia and – at the time – unable to read or write. That he would later to go on to accumulate 20 honorary doctorates and become a professor of creative writing is only one way, and in my view not the best one, of measuring his talent. The man was the late, great poet Benjamin Zephaniah . And he had been nothing but transparent about his lack of credentials. In fact it was his background that made him eligible for this fellowship, which was designed to reach out to somebody in the community who didn’t have a degree, to give them the opportunity to have a connection with the university. Continue reading...

data.title: Heard about the ‘luteal uglies’? Women know more about our hormones than ever – and that’s beautiful | Rhiannon Lucy Cosslett
data.description: When I was younger, female biology was seen as something to be overcome. Now we can talk about the reality of living in our bodies Have you got the “ luteal uglies ”? I’m not trying to insult you, merely deploying the latest hormonal buzz phrase on social media, which refers to the phase in a woman’s cycle, two or so weeks between ovulation and menstruation, when she apparently feels at her lowest and most unattractive due to a drop in oestrogen levels. Women’s hormones have become trending topics and, as someone who only found out what a “luteal phase” is when she Googled it, mid-fertility panic, in her late 20s, I am somewhat in awe of the expertise with which younger women discuss their menstrual cycles now. They’re just so incredibly literate. Rhiannon Lucy Cosslett is a Guardian columnist and the author of Female, Nude Continue reading...

data.title: I was enjoying growing vegetables. Then the climate crisis raised its ugly head | Bim Adewunmi
data.description: My child and I were bonding over our hit-and-miss approach to reaping crops. But with heatwaves pushing more of Britain into drought, it’s starting to feel like a luxury we can’t afford For the first time in my life, I live in a home that has real outdoor space. What a concept! There are no downsides to a garden. Back in spring, I made grand plans – I watched all the TikToks, I bought seeds and trays and pots and grow bags, I ordered soil, a trowel and a watering can. I knew what I was after: super-tiny-scale subsistence farming with a side of Zen. A little fruit, a little veg, lots of flowers to attract pollinators . And I knew I wanted my elder child to gain an understanding of how things come to be and how to cope if and when they fail. We love a tomato side salad, so that was the first thing we attempted. The seedlings flourished and then died in the first heatwave of the season. An omen, surely. The dahlias, ranunculus and freesias refused to grow, let alone bloom. My enthusiasm began to wane. data.title: Millions of US tax dollars sent to rightwing European thinktanks. Did any Trump supporters vote for that? | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: It’s a great betrayal: poor communities neglected while multimillionaires peddle a global Maga agenda. How is that America first? “THE CORRUPTION IS AT LEVELS RARELY SEEN BEFORE,” Donald Trump posted on Truth Social in February 2025 . He was not referring to his own administration, but to the US Agency for International Development (USAID). “CLOSE IT DOWN!” the president added. Just a few hours later USAID was in effect closed down, with most of the staff placed on indefinite administration leave . This was framed as part of Trump’s “America first” agenda. Deep in the final set of the first-round match at the Canadian Open against Térence Atmane just over a week ago, 15 months of pent up emotion erupted. Two games from defeat, Draper spent the entire changeover in tears . This was a devastating and alarming sight. Injuries had already defined so much of Draper’s career, but the uncertainty of trying to recover from a bone bruise injury to his left arm over the past year has been more challenging than anything he has experienced. All of his efforts since last July have been focused on trying to find a way to compete consistently at the highest level again, to no avail. Continue reading...

data.title: Humpbacks return to Rio: the whales are back from the brink of extinction – but will tourism help or hinder?
data.description: The gigantic aquatic acrobats are exciting Brazil’s tourists as numbers recover from whaling. But some marine biologists question how booming tourism and conservation can coexist The anticipation is palpable onboard the Boaventura II as the yacht sets off from Rio de Janeiro at sunrise. Once beyond the Cagarras Islands, rocky outcrops just three miles off Ipanema beach, the group gathers at the bow and starts scanning the horizon. They do not have to wait long. “Eleven o’clock!” someone calls out, as a pod of bottlenose dolphins appears, playfully diving in and out of the water. Then, two spouts of vapour hanging in the air signal the reason for the outing: a pair of humpback whales. The majestic mammals surface to breathe with an unhurried chuff, before revealing the underside of their fluke as they dive back underwater. Continue reading...

data.title: The Plot review – exploding myths in an hour of gunpowder and treason
data.description: Summerhall, Edinburgh Set in purgatory, Emma Howlett’s two-hander rethinks the national intrigue with 5 November Never play with matches is good advice – especially when gunpowder is involved. That the historical figures of Thomas and Robert Wintour begin this two-hander testing each other’s capacity to endure a naked flame suggests they have a high tolerance for risk. It is not clear if there are still explosives lying around, but they should know better. Not that it matters any more. These two Catholic brothers have sussed they must be in purgatory, their plot to blow up parliament having been foiled. Their accounts of what happened next are fuzzy, but they both remember being sentenced to death. They are not happy about their fate, but feel even more sympathy for the mercenary stooge known as Guy Fawkes, who has had to carry the can. Continue reading...

data.title: Why we’re going back to the games of our youth
data.description: As millennials return to the games of their youth, remakes of Star Fox and Halo suggest there is still plenty to learn from the past • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Retro collections are started, or resumed; jewel-cases of PS1 classics or cardboard boxes with SNES or Mega Drive games have started to colonise the living-room shelves. People are replaying things from their university days, or sticking to comfort games such as Stardew Valley. data.title: The Wrong Girls review – Kristen Stewart fumbles through forgettable stoner comedy
data.description: First time director Dylan Meyer’s female twist on the genre is let down by silly stereotypes and jokes that land with a thud Want to feel old? Superbad turns 20 next year. It’s been decades since the stoner comedy ruled the box office. In fact, the genre’s best theatrically released film of recent years – the hilarious buddy movie One of Them Days – didn’t feature any weed smoking at all despite hitting all the usual outlandish beats of a stoner flick. If the streaming success of Hulu’s recent R-rated bong-ripper Pizza Movie is anything to go by, audiences would rather watch this particular strain of movie on the couch where they can spark up in peace. The Wrong Girls aims to reverse that trend with a nationwide US theatrical rollout by Neon, the arty distributor which propelled Parasite and Anora to Oscar glory. Best friends Molly ( Alia Shawkat ) and Frankie ( Kristen Stewart ) live in a PeeWee’s Playhouse-coded stoner cave with macrame decor, a life-size cutout of Céline Dion, multiple cat towers and a contraption called the bong-o-tron – a complex rig of tubes and bubbling conical flasks – that fills the entirety of their coffee table. Being high all the time gives them a daffy kind of magical thinking, as they drive around town belting out power ballads and imagine that they are under the ocean with all manner of friendly sea creatures. Continue reading...

data.title: My Brilliant Career review – Netflix’s take on this Australian classic is sassy and steamy – but a tad syrupy
data.description: Philippa Northeast is entertaining as Sybylla Melvyn in this adaptation of Miles Franklin’s 1901 novel that has more erotica and a more pronounced love triangle It’s difficult to believe that Miles Franklin’s wonderfully lively and rebellious novel My Brilliant Career is 125 years old: its prose crackles with life and energy, and the words leap off the page. Notwithstanding some inevitably dated turns of phrase (though I, for one, feel it’s time to return “what the deuce!” to daily conversations), the book feels like it could have been written yesterday. The story is centred around Sybylla Melvyn, a bullheaded author determined to write her own story – literally and otherwise – in a deeply patriarchal world that would prefer her to settle down, shut up and take a man’s hand in marriage. Whereas Gillian Armstrong’s 1979 film adaptation is a class act, elegant and stately, Netflix’s new six-part series is, perhaps predictably, steamier and more juiced up, with at times Mills & Boon-ish vibes. There’s more erotica, a wilder tone and a more pronounced love triangle for Sybylla, played by Philippa Northeast. Unfortunately, it’s also a tad syrupy and wishy-washy, particularly towards the end (this review encompasses every episode) – the show even deploys one of those cloying photo album-like montages of key moments: the visual equivalent of Green Day’s Good Riddance. Continue reading...

data.title: Don’t Say Good Luck review – high-school musical weepie puts Sunny Sandler in the spotlight
data.description: A mother’s illness threatens to overshadow a stagestruck teen’s big break in a school production Do you, like me, have a soft spot for both high-school angst and Broadway showtunes – and maybe Douglas Goodhart’s amusing Master It! Insta reels on how to make it in musical theatre? Then you might find yourself giving a pass to this sugary but heartfelt teen weepie from director and co-writer Julia Hart, co-produced by Adam Sandler and starring his daughter Sunny Sandler. She plays Soph, the shy theatre kid who unexpectedly gets the lead in her school production of the musical Waitress. Her devoted mom Elizabeth ( Melanie Lynskey ) has cancer, and thinks she should maybe wait until after the run to tell Soph the awful truth, so as not to spoil her big moment. But will that be ... too late? Continue reading...

data.title: Steal This Story, Please! review – Amy Goodman, stalwart of the American left, shows her teeth
data.description: This comprehensive documentary about the Democracy Now! radio show host and seasoned investigative reporter takes in a massacre in East Timor, the actions of oil giants and a flustered Bill Clinton as it reflects her vital work Before there was Michael Moore, there was campaigning journalist Amy Goodman … and even if Moore seems to have gone a little quiet, Goodman is still there, doggedly asking questions, an earnest gadfly buzzing around the flinching faces of Trump placemen, challenging and provoking and annoying. With her listener-funded syndicated radio show Democracy Now!, on the air since 1996, Goodman is flying the flag for journalism of the unfashionably homespun progressive left, while America’s corporate news media are sheepishly capitulating to their tech oligarch owners. This documentary from Carl Deal and Tia Lessin is a portrait of Goodman and her life and times. The title is her somewhat ironic mantra: please, everybody, by all means steal our stories about corruption and demagoguery. Sadly, the big news media are often uninterested (though sometimes they are forced to follow stories broken by Goodman and her team). In fact, the real demand is addressed to their audience: buy this story, please. Democracy Now! accepts no ads or sponsorship, and it relies on money from viewers, listeners and readers of its website, although this documentary is silent on how much it needs annually and how the cash is solicited. Continue reading...

data.title: A History of the Novel in Britain by Philip Hensher review – a masterpiece of criticism
data.description: This joyous book takes readers on a literary adventure across 300 years of fiction, from Defoe to Zadie Smith In his opening paragraph, Philip Hensher declares that a novel not only “tells a good story” but is a good story in itself. We could extend that neat formula to include this book, which is not only a masterful account of fiction since 1719, when Daniel Defoe set Robinson Crusoe down on his desert island, but is itself a wonderful read. There is nothing dreary here; no sense of being back in the seminar room taking notes. Instead it is 600 pages of deep pleasure, an excuse to revisit old literary loves and be reminded of ones that have slipped from view. Hensher is smart enough to know why his book works so well and vain enough to tell us. The usual methodology for a survey is to assemble a roster of academics and invite them to trot out a chapter on their specialism, whether that be “Thomas Hardy” or “High Modernism”. The result is a series of silos, with little sense of historical connection or intellectual unfolding. Hensher, by contrast, gives us a joined-up account of creative call and response. Equally crucial to this project’s success is Hensher’s own experience as a novelist. He brings a practitioner’s informed eye to such questions as why some chapters in Dickens’s Dombey and Son are in the present tense or how Henry James pulls off free indirect speech in What Maisie Knew. Continue reading...

data.title: Something Like Happiness by Tom Newlands review – a tender take on hard times, anger and autism
data.description: A twentysomething Scottish couple care for their autistic son in the bleak follow-up to Only Here, Only Now Frazer and Caitlin have been emotionally entwined since schooldays. Now in their mid-20s, and parents of a five-year-old, they live in a grotty flat in a Scottish new town – the faded posters read “Happiness, Here” – that has crumbled into decay. Jobs are scarce and unrewarding; little Jamie, who has autism, is silent; and the pressure is starting to tell. Frazer’s adored Caitlin is “beautiful and driven”, fit, petite – and a rageaholic. At her mildest she’s irritated and unreasonable, at her worst violent and intimidating. She is incensed at Frazer’s refusal to move from their mould-infested block to the new council house they’ve been assigned. Apex Court is where he was brought up, filled with relics of his dead parents, and it’s the only home his son has ever known. “You’ve become the sad sack guardian of a bunch of shite that belonged to your parents, including their hovel of a flat,” Cait sneers. Continue reading...

data.title: Carcass Clad: stifling tank combat promises tension, terror and surprising laughs
data.description: After the success of space horror Mouthwashing, Swedish developer Wrong Organ has created a Battlefield-inspired co-op with a supernatural twist ‘Claustrophobic”, “oppressive”, “pretty depressing” – these are the words Jeffrey Tomec and Dave van Egdom volunteer when I ask them to reflect on their work as part of Swedish indie developer Wrong Organ . I’d add “nightmare-inducing”, too. Their last game, Mouthwashing , was an acclaimed work of horror storytelling set on a scuttled space freighter, in which players uncover the horrible things its desperate crew have done to each other. When you’re planning a follow-up to something so pitilessly nasty, how do you raise the stakes? Well, you could set the entire game in the stifling crew compartment of a heavily armoured tank, a coffin-like interior you share with two other players as you co-operatively attempt to pilot your beleaguered war machine to safety through the crumbling remains of a city in enemy territory. data.title: Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls review – an anime-style rumble that’s rooting for you
data.description: PlayStation 5, PC; Arc System Works/Sony Interactive Entertainment With tremendous visuals and accessible controls, this superhero-themed fighter has the chops to inspire a new generation of champs Arriving at the turn of the millennium and the twilight of the video arcade, Marvel vs Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes has long been a high-water mark for fighting games, with no heir apparent; its massive, colourful roster and frenetic, spectacular combos have lured newcomers and elite competitors alike. Developer Arc System Works, a fan-favourite studio famous for its hyper-fluid and extremely technical anime-style fighting games, has been on a long journey to usurp Capcom’s throne. With Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, it may have finally achieved this difficult task. Marvel Tōkon is less an attempt to recreate a Marvel vs Capcom-esque phenomenon out of whole cloth, and more a thoughtful evolution of the developer’s previous riffs on the formula such as 2018’s BlazBlue: Cross Tag Battle and Dragon Ball FighterZ, building on its low-floor, high-ceiling approach. Simplified inputs allow players to execute combos and finishers with a single button, which gives novices the confidence to keep playing and inspires them to study and improve – because when anyone can pull off a flashy ultimate skill or EX attack, strategy and mastery take on a premium. And Marvel Tōkon has great depths to plumb. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Today’s Brazilians have no idea what it feels like to lose democracy’: Joyce Moreno on her battles to become a Latin musical great
data.description: After her defiant femininity outraged many in Brazil, she lived through a military dictatorship and was boycotted for years. But after more than 30 albums, she explains how she kept going At 78, Joyce Moreno is one of Brazil’s musical icons, but for decades that status seemed far from assured: this headstrong singer, guitarist and composer was frequently viewed as a threat by her country’s establishment. Aged 19, the reaction to her song Me Disseram – which began “I was told my man didn’t love me” – almost torpedoed her career before it even started. “I’d often heard the expression ‘my man’ sung by Billie Holiday and Edith Piaf, so for me it was normal,” she says. “But I was a beach girl from Ipanema, writing and singing in the first person. People were shocked.” Then, inspired by trailblazing actor Leila Diniz (“her liberal attitudes lost her jobs”), Moreno refused requests that she “dress like a sexy bimbo”, and endured male critics who thought her music “too good to have been written by a woman”. When, in 1980, she discovered that her label had given another female singer the blueprints for songs she had written, she “looked for a lawyer, of course” and successfully sued; in her memoir she claims she was then boycotted by Brazil’s major record companies for a decade. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘If we exhibited all the Balkan jokes, we wouldn’t have opened’: a trip to Slovenia’s Bullshit Museum
data.description: In the heart of old Ljubljana, a mannequin with a bucket on its head welcomes visitors to a new and ambitious project – a museum focusing on the varied and sometimes antagonistic humour of the former Yugoslavia On the main promenade along the river that runs through Ljubljana, Slovenia’s capital, tourists stop to photograph a mannequin with a bucket on its head. Dressed in a pistachio jacket and red leggings, the figure sits at a table in front of one of the houses in the historic Old Town, staring at a spilled cup of Turkish coffee, popular with Slovenes and with the other Balkan and central European citizens with whom they shared a country, until it collapsed in the early 1990s. A large sign in the background reads: “Bullshit Museum: The world is off the rails, and so are we. Yebiga !” Yebiga , which can be loosely translated as “fuck it”, or “screw it”, is the red thread running through the museum that was launched in May and consists of five small rooms filled with mannequins wearing odd accessories, AI-generated images of laughing characters and scenes accompanying some of the jokes, framed or displayed on cardboard screens. The word encompasses the heart of Balkan humour, says the museum’s founder, Borut Kokelj, who wears a T-shirt emblazoned with the words: “What part of yebiga don’t you understand?” Continue reading...

data.title: From sensation to spectacular, to silence: the strange history of Coleridge-Taylor’s Song of Hiawatha
data.description: Chances to hear Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s choral masterpiece in concert are rare. Ahead of its belated Edinburgh festival premiere with the Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal, we look at the epic work - and its epic baggage The Song of Hiawatha, Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s setting of Henry Longfellow’s poem, comes to the Edinburgh international festival next week . It’s the first time the work will be performed there, a very belated premiere for the three-part cantata that sealed the composer’s reputation nationally and internationally, inspiring Coleridge-Taylor societies in the US, and making him the world’s best-known Black classical composer of the Edwardian era, before his tragically early death at the age of just 37 in 1912 . The performance history of The Song of Hiawatha makes for an astounding story. In the early years of the 20th century the work quickly became a sensation, with hundreds of performances on both sides of the Atlantic. In 1924, and then every year from 1926 to 1939 , the Royal Albert Hall housed a spectacular and vast staging that involved around 1,000 performers – 200 dancers and hundreds of singers of the Royal Choral Society – dressed up to play out a series of exoticised and racialised caricatures to be part of the pageant of Hiawatha, Minnehaha and their tribespeople. The Mohawk chief also performed in the shows, granting an apparent authenticity to The Song of Hiawatha’s dramaturgy. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Feminists need to push back’: how did the women’s movement become so divided – and how can it reunite?
data.description: Just a few years ago, women would fight for other women whatever their background or politics. Today, many loudly dismiss the struggles of those who are not like them. But the solidarity is still there, if you look hard enough One June day in 2015, I stood outside Yarl’s Wood immigration removal centre near Bedford and heard the women inside singing. “Set her free,” said the graffiti on the walls. “Shut it down.” I had often visited the centre and heard the desperate stories of women who were held inside it. But that day felt hopeful rather than despairing, as hundreds of women – refugees, campaigners, lawyers, members of parliament, actors, writers – gathered around the centre to demand freedom for the women locked up. When I set up the organisation Women for Refugee Women , I was driven by my faith in solidarity among women. The organisation works with women seeking asylum in Britain to tell their stories and campaign for justice and safety. For years I felt that faith being proved in practice. Women turned up for other women at events and demonstrations; they were volunteering and campaigning, marching and supporting. Continue reading...

data.title: Katendrecht: Rotterdam’s sailors’ quarter reinvented as cultural hub
data.description: The regeneration of historic warehouses has transformed this former red-light district into one of the port city’s most vibrant areas A thin peninsula just south of Rotterdam’s centre, Katendrecht was once at the heart of the world’s busiest port, home to continental Europe’s first Chinatown and a lively sailors’ quarter. Its later reputation as a red light district has been shrugged off – part of the city’s wider reinvention in the aftermath of extensive second world war bombing. Continue reading...

data.title: How to use up parmesan rind to make pesto – recipe | Waste not
data.description: Why waste the tastiest bit of the cheese? Although parmesan rind is tough, it has just as much, if not more flavour than the cheese from inside the wheel itself. It can be used just as it is to flavour stock or risi e bisi (Venetian pea risotto), but grating it opens up a whole range of other uses, such as in my mac and cheese “rinds ” and today’s parmesan rind pesto. The flavour is very powerful, though, so add it to taste: you may find that you need a lot less than you think you do. Continue reading...

data.title: Emiko Davies’ Japanese curry rice (kare raisu) – recipe
data.description: The Australian-born cook and author shares her recipe for a thick, fragrant Japanese curry – with one secret ingredient Japanese curry – kare raisu in Japanese – is unlike any “curry” you might know from south Asian countries. That is partly because of the nature of yoshoku (western-influenced) cuisine but also because it made a roundabout route to Japan, via the British Royal Navy during the Meiji Restoration, a period when India was under British colonial rule. It arrived in the form of British “C&B” curry powder, so it was considered western food, not Indian. Curry became a staple in the Japanese naval and army kitchens at the turn of the century and this in turn brought curry into homes and even into school lunches. Today, it is considered a national dish. Japanese curry needed to be thick enough so that it could be easily eaten with rice, with the help of a spoon. This can be achieved with a French-style roux base of butter, flour and liquid, or it can be thickened in a more Japanese style using a potato starchy slurry right at the end of cooking, which is my preference. Then there is the spice mix. Today, Japanese S&B curry powder is one of the best known, which contains 17 spices such as turmeric, coriander, fenugreek, cumin, cinnamon, fennel, ginger and star anise. Continue reading...

data.title: Louisiana creates 1,170 acres of wetlands; shrimp and crabs return to restored habitat after a year
data.description: Louisiana’s Upper Barataria Marsh Creation Project has restored 1,170 acres of new wetland habitat in the Barataria Basin. One year after construction, white and brown shrimp, blue crab and red drum are using the restored marsh and water features. The project aims to rebuild coastal ecosystems damaged by decades of land loss and the Deepwater Horizon oil spill.

data.title: Quote by Voltaire: 'Life is a shipwreck, but we must not forget to sing in the lifeboats'
data.description: Life often throws insurmountable challenges our way, yet how we respond is within our control. A saying mistakenly linked to Voltaire beautifully encapsulates this spirit of resilience. This notion complements Viktor Frankl's concept of tragic optimism, proposing that we can find joy amid adversity. Embracing radical acceptance allows us to confront our circumstances, paving the way to discover meaning and happiness even in the darkest times.

data.title: Quote by Montesquieu: 'Success of most things depends upon knowing how long it will take to succeed'
data.description: Jeff Bezos led Amazon by prioritizing a long-term vision rather than chasing short-term gains. This perspective aligns with Montesquieu's philosophy that success is often a lengthy journey. Misjudging project timeframes can lead to distress and hasty strategy changes. Insights from modern behavioral science highlight the planning fallacy and sunk cost biases. To excel in any domain, it is crucial to accurately grasp how long true mastery takes.

data.translatedDescription: A study published in “Nature” highlights that artificial intelligence will make it possible to recover several billion barrels from existing deposits, reduce drilling costs and exploit resources previously considered unprofitable.

data.title: L’administration Trump annule un rapport de référence sur l’Arctique, une nouvelle atteinte à la science du climat aux Etats-Unis
data.description: Publié chaque année depuis 2006, ce document est très estimé par la communauté scientifique, qui subit l’offensive climatosceptique du gouvernement américain.
data.translatedTitle: Trump administration cancels landmark Arctic report, further attack on US climate science
data.translatedDescription: Published every year since 2006, this document is highly esteemed by the scientific community, which is suffering from the climate skeptic offensive of the American government.

data.title: Le PSG conserve son titre dans la Supercoupe d’Europe en venant à bout d’Aston Villa
data.description: Bien que bousculés par les Anglais, les hommes de Luis Enrique sont parvenus à l’emporter grâce à des buts de Khvicha Kvaratskhelia et de Désiré Doué, mercredi, à Salzbourg (Autriche).
data.translatedTitle: PSG retains its title in the European Super Cup by defeating Aston Villa
data.translatedDescription: Although pushed by the English, Luis Enrique's men managed to win thanks to goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué on Wednesday in Salzburg (Austria).

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : selon Volodymyr Zelensky, Kiev a besoin d’au moins 5 % des missiles Patriot de Washington pour contrer les attaques balistiques russes
data.description: Avec un tel niveau d’achat de missiles intercepteurs, « nous passerons l’hiver et sauverons des vies », a déclaré, à CNN, le président ukrainien, précisant en recevoir actuellement 1 % seulement.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, war in Ukraine: Volodymyr Zelensky says kyiv needs at least 5% of Washington's Patriot missiles to counter Russian ballistic attacks
data.translatedDescription: With such a level of purchase of interceptor missiles, “we will get through the winter and save lives,” the Ukrainian president told CNN, specifying that he currently only receives 1%.

data.title: Chez easyJet, la grève des personnels de cabine français en plein week-end du 15 août pourrait être très suivie
data.description: Les syndicats des hôtesses et stewards de la compagnie à bas coût en France appellent à un arrêt de travail, samedi et dimanche, après l’échec de discussions, mercredi, avec la direction sur l’amélioration des conditions de travail.
data.translatedTitle: At easyJet, the French cabin crew strike in the middle of the weekend of August 15 could be very popular
data.translatedDescription: The unions of hostesses and stewards of the low-cost airline in France are calling for a work stoppage, Saturday and Sunday, after the failure of discussions on Wednesday with management on improving working conditions.

data.title: Fraude bancaire par « SIM swap » : l’opérateur téléphonique et la banque condamnés
data.description: Une victime dont on avait usurpé l’identité et qui s’était fait dérober 16 964 euros a été indemnisée par BNP Paribas et Free Mobile.
data.translatedTitle: Bank fraud by “SIM swap”: the telephone operator and the bank convicted
data.translatedDescription: A victim whose identity had been stolen and who had 16,964 euros stolen was compensated by BNP Paribas and Free Mobile.

data.title: Donald Trump annonce le départ de sa porte-parole, Karoline Leavitt
data.description: Cette républicaine de 28 ans, plus jeune personne jamais nommée à ce poste très exposé, a piloté une stratégie de communication agressive, riche en attaques contre les médias traditionnels.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump announces the departure of his spokesperson, Karoline Leavitt
data.translatedDescription: This 28-year-old Republican, the youngest person ever appointed to this highly exposed position, has piloted an aggressive communications strategy, rife with attacks on traditional media.

data.title: Au Venezuela, le pouvoir et l’opposition annoncent des points d’accord autour d’une réforme judiciaire
data.description: A l’issue d’une semaine de pourparlers à Caracas, les deux parties ont aussi déclaré s’unir pour demander à récupérer des fonds gelés au Royaume-Uni en raison de sanctions contre le pays sous la présidence de Nicolas Maduro.
data.translatedTitle: In Venezuela, the government and the opposition announce points of agreement around judicial reform
data.translatedDescription: At the end of a week of talks in Caracas, the two parties also declared that they were uniting to request the recovery of funds frozen in the United Kingdom due to sanctions against the country under the presidency of Nicolas Maduro.

data.title: NBA : les Los Angeles Lakers vont être vendus pour 12,5 milliards de dollars
data.description: Selon le média américain ESPN, la célèbre franchise de basket devrait être rachetée par Joshua Kushner, frère du gendre de Donald Trump, et par l’ancien patron de Disney, Bob Iger. L’équipe avait déjà changé de propriétaire en 2025.
data.translatedTitle: NBA: Los Angeles Lakers to be sold for $12.5 billion
data.translatedDescription: According to the American media ESPN, the famous basketball franchise should be bought by Joshua Kushner, brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law, and by the former boss of Disney, Bob Iger. The team had already changed ownership in 2025.

data.title: La Colombie autorise des opérations antidrogue conjointes avec les Etats-Unis
data.description: Elu sur la promesse d’éradiquer les groupes impliqués dans le narcotrafic, le nouveau président colombien, Abelardo de la Espriella, est un allié de son homologue américain, Donald Trump. Cet accord, annoncé mercredi 12 août, permet à Washington d’accélérer sa lutte contre le trafic de drogue en Amérique latine.
data.translatedTitle: Colombia authorizes joint counter-drug operations with the United States
data.translatedDescription: Elected on the promise of eradicating groups involved in drug trafficking, the new Colombian president, Abelardo de la Espriella, is an ally of his American counterpart, Donald Trump. This agreement, announced on Wednesday August 12, allows Washington to accelerate its fight against drug trafficking in Latin America.

data.title: Boeing condamné à verser 29 millions de dollars à la famille d’une victime du crash en 2019 du 737 MAX
data.description: Un jury américain a accordé cette indemnisation à la famille de Michael Ryan, ingénieur irlandais de l’ONU qui faisait partie des 157 personnes tuées dans l’accident du vol ET302 d’Ethiopian Airlines, le 10 mars 2019.
data.translatedTitle: Boeing ordered to pay $29 million to family of 2019 737 MAX crash victim
data.translatedDescription: A US jury awarded this compensation to the family of Michael Ryan, an Irish UN engineer who was among the 157 people killed in the crash of Ethiopian Airlines flight ET302 on March 10, 2019.

data.title: Maximilian Krah: Haftbefehl gegen AfD-Politiker im Streit mit Jan Böhmermann
data.description: Der AfD-Bundestagsabgeordnete wollte dem Satiriker bestimmte Aussagen gerichtlich untersagen. Doch er verlor und muss die Kosten tragen. Weil er diese nicht komplett zahlt, hat das Amtsgericht Chemnitz nach SPIEGEL-Informationen Konsequenzen gezogen.
data.translatedTitle: Maximilian Krah: Arrest warrant against AfD politician in dispute with Jan Böhmermann
data.translatedDescription: The AfD member of the Bundestag wanted to legally ban the satirist from making certain statements. But he lost and has to bear the costs. Because he did not pay this in full, the Chemnitz district court took action, according to SPIEGEL information.

data.title: News: Mehr Rechte für Geheimdienste, AfD-Wahlkampf in Sachsen-Anhalt, Nigel Farage gegen das Mülleimergesicht
data.description: Deutschland soll »echte Geheimdienste« bekommen. AfD-Spitzenkandidat Siegmund versucht sich als netter Kerl zu inszenieren. Und: Mr. Brexit muss gegen einen Mülleimer gewinnen. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagmorgen.
data.translatedTitle: News: More rights for secret services, AfD election campaign in Saxony-Anhalt, Nigel Farage against the trash can face
data.translatedDescription: Germany should get “real secret services”. AfD top candidate Siegmund tries to present himself as a nice guy. And: Mr. Brexit has to win against a trash can. This is the situation on Thursday morning.

data.title: MDR-Wahlarena »Fakt ist«: Echte Bürger stellen echte Fragen – und die Politiker weichen aus
data.description: Ein ratloser Syrer, Eiertanz um die Brandmauer und sehr viele »Grundursachen«: Der MDR-Wahlabend zu Sachsen-Anhalt hat mehr enthüllt, als manchem Kandidaten lieb sein dürfte.
data.translatedTitle: MDR election arena “The fact is”: Real citizens ask real questions – and the politicians avoid them
data.translatedDescription: A perplexed Syrian, dancing around the firewall and a lot of "root causes": the MDR election evening in Saxony-Anhalt revealed more than some candidates would like.

data.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Bündnispläne bei AfD-Sieg - Was wirklich hinter Sahra Wagenknechts Taktik steckt
data.description: Bei der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt droht nach dem möglichen Erfolg der AfD Koalitionschaos: Sahra Wagenknecht wittert ihre Chance und will als Königsmacherin auftreten. Kann das gelingen?
data.translatedTitle: Saxony-Anhalt: Alliance plans in the event of AfD victory - What is really behind Sahra Wagenknecht's tactics
data.translatedDescription: In the state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, there is a risk of coalition chaos following the possible success of the AfD: Sahra Wagenknecht senses her chance and wants to act as kingmaker. Can that succeed?

data.title: Reform der Geheimdienste: Mehr Macht für BND und Verfassungsschutz, mehr Aufsicht
data.description: Es ist richtig, dass die deutschen Geheimdienste mehr Befugnisse bekommen. Die Gefahr durch Russland ist real. Doch mehr Macht erfordert auch mehr Kontrolle.
data.translatedTitle: Reform of the secret services: More power for the BND and the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, more supervision
data.translatedDescription: It is true that the German secret services are given more powers. The threat from Russia is real. But more power also requires more control.

ner.label: ORG

data.title: Karoline Leavitt geht – Donald Trump braucht ein neues Sprachrohr
data.description: Als bisher jüngste Sprecherin im Weißen Haus vertrat Karoline Leavitt den US-Präsidenten mit voller Überzeugung und rabiatem Ton. Jetzt hört sie auf, während Donald Trump in immer größeren Schwierigkeiten steckt.
data.translatedTitle: Karoline Leavitt is leaving – Donald Trump needs a new mouthpiece
data.translatedDescription: As the youngest spokeswoman to date in the White House, Karoline Leavitt represented the US President with full conviction and a rabid tone. Now it's stopping while Donald Trump is in deeper trouble.

data.title: CIA zweifelte offenbar an iranischer Bedrohung für Trump
data.description: Der US-Präsident wurde auf dem Rückweg vom Nato-Gipfel per Catering-Container in einen Militärflieger geschmuggelt. Nun berichten US-Medien: Das Täuschungsmanöver ging womöglich auf aufgebauschte Hinweise aus Israel zurück.
data.translatedTitle: CIA apparently doubted that there was an Iranian threat to Trump
data.translatedDescription: The US President was smuggled onto a military plane in a catering container on the way back from the NATO summit. Now US media are reporting: The deception may have been based on exaggerated information from Israel.

data.title: USA: ICE-Agenten sollen Elektroschock-Handschuhe bekommen
data.description: Die Handschuhe werden per Tastendruck aktiviert – und geben beim Anfassen von Personen Elektroschocks ab: ICE will seine Mitarbeiter mit neuen Geräten ausstatten und spricht von »Deeskalation«. Die Opposition bewertet das anders.
data.translatedTitle: USA: ICE agents should be given electric shock gloves
data.translatedDescription: The gloves are activated at the touch of a button - and give off electric shocks when you touch people: ICE wants to equip its employees with new devices and speaks of "de-escalation". The opposition sees it differently.

data.title: Waldbrände in Deutschland und Europa: Wo es gerade brennt - Live-Grafiken
data.description: Wie außergewöhnlich ist die aktuelle Waldbrandsaison, wo brennt es derzeit und wie viele Flächen sind den Flammen schon zum Opfer gefallen? Der fortwährend aktualisierte Überblick in Karten und Grafiken.
data.translatedTitle: Forest fires in Germany and Europe: Where things are currently burning - live graphics
data.translatedDescription: How unusual is the current forest fire season, where is the fire currently burning and how many areas have already fallen victim to the flames? The continually updated overview of maps and graphics.

data.title: Wetter in Deutschland: Es wird wieder richtig heiß – bis zu 37 Grad erwartet
data.description: Deutschland stehen die nächsten Hitzetage bevor. Für das Wochenende wird jedoch ein Wetterumschwung vorhergesagt, mit teils kräftigen Schauern und Gewittern.
data.translatedTitle: Weather in Germany: It's getting really hot again - up to 37 degrees expected
data.translatedDescription: Germany is facing the next hot days. However, a change in the weather is forecast for the weekend, with some heavy showers and thunderstorms.

data.title: Perseiden-Sternschnuppen: Kaum ist die Sonnenfinsternis vorbei, beginnt das nächste Himmelsspektakel
data.description: Darf’s noch ein Wunsch mehr sein? In der vergangenen, mondlosen Nacht erreichte der Sternschnuppenstrom der Perseiden seinen Höhepunkt. Fast überall in Deutschland herrschte exzellente Sicht.
data.translatedTitle: Perseid shooting stars: As soon as the solar eclipse is over, the next celestial spectacle begins
data.translatedDescription: Can you wish for one more thing? Last moonless night, the Perseid meteor shower reached its peak. There was excellent visibility almost everywhere in Germany.

data.title: Sonnenfinsternis: So erlebten Millionen Menschen das Himmelsereignis
data.description: Millionen Menschen quer durch Europa starrten in den Himmel – und wurden nicht enttäuscht. Das Spektakel am Himmel lieferte faszinierende Bilder, die besten im Video.
data.translatedTitle: Solar eclipse: This is how millions of people experienced the celestial event
data.translatedDescription: Millions of people across Europe stared at the sky - and were not disappointed. The spectacle in the sky provided fascinating images, the best in the video.

data.title: Beste Feinde Musk und Trump: Ein riesiger Fabrikneubau als Signal ans Weiße Haus
data.translatedTitle: Best enemies Musk and Trump: A huge new factory building as a signal to the White House

data.title: Mord an Rob und Michele Reiner: Sohn Nick soll seinen Eltern aufgelauert haben
data.description: Der Sohn des Hollywoodpaars Rob und Michele Reiner steht wegen Mordes an seinen Eltern vor Gericht. Eine Anklageschrift legt nun neue Vorwürfe gegen den 32-Jährigen offen.
data.translatedTitle: Murder of Rob and Michele Reiner: Son Nick is said to have ambushed his parents
data.translatedDescription: The son of Hollywood couple Rob and Michele Reiner is on trial for the murder of his parents. An indictment now reveals new allegations against the 32-year-old.

data.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Streit um Ausladung von CDU und Linken aus TV-Runde
data.description: Die Spitzenkandidaten der CDU und der Linken in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern sind zu einer Fernsehdebatte erst ein-, dann wieder ausgeladen worden. Beide geben nun Ministerpräsidentin Manuela Schwesig die Schuld.
data.translatedTitle: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: Dispute over disinvitement of the CDU and the Left from the TV group
data.translatedDescription: The top candidates of the CDU and the Left in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania were first invited to a television debate and then disinvited again. Both now blame Prime Minister Manuela Schwesig.

data.title: Fort Hood in Texas: Zwei Tote nach Absturz eines US-Militärhubschraubers
data.description: In der Nähe eines Stützpunkts der US-Landstreitkräfte in Texas verunglückt ein Apache-Hubschrauber. Beide Besatzungsmitglieder sterben. Der Absturz löst zudem einen Waldbrand aus.
data.translatedTitle: Fort Hood in Texas: Two dead after a US military helicopter crashes
data.translatedDescription: An Apache helicopter crashes near a US land force base in Texas. Both crew members die. The crash also triggers a forest fire.

data.title: WNBA: »MAGA-Barbie«, Trans-Hass und »White Privilege« – wie Sophie Cunningham den US-Basketball ins Chaos stürzt
data.description: Die Debatten über die US-Liga WNBA drehen sich um alles außer Basketball: ob trans Frauen gegen Frauen spielen dürfen oder ob weiße Spielerinnen bevorzugt werden. Das Gesicht der Absurdität ist Sophie Cunningham.
data.translatedTitle: WNBA: “MAGA-Barbie”, trans hate and “white privilege” – how Sophie Cunningham is throwing US basketball into chaos
data.translatedDescription: The debates about the US league WNBA revolve around everything except basketball: whether trans women are allowed to play against women or whether white players are preferred. The face of absurdity is Sophie Cunningham.

data.title: Fußball: Spanier Xavi Hernández wird neuer Trainer der Niederländer
data.description: Die Fußballauswahl der Niederlande hat einen neuen Trainer. Der frühere Barcelona-Star Xavi Hernández soll das Team bis zur Weltmeisterschaft 2030 coachen. Erster Gegner: die deutsche Mannschaft.
data.translatedTitle: Football: Spaniard Xavi Hernández becomes the new coach of the Dutch
data.translatedDescription: The Netherlands football team has a new coach. Former Barcelona star Xavi Hernández is set to coach the team until the 2030 World Cup. First opponent: the German team.

data.title: Schwimm-EM in Paris: Johannes Liebmann holt Gold mit Europarekord über 800 Meter
data.description: Schneller war noch kein Europäer über diese Distanz: Nachwuchsstar Johannes Liebmann gewann in Paris über 800 Meter Freistil. Und das vor seinem eigenen Teamkollegen Sven Schwarz.
data.translatedTitle: European Swimming Championships in Paris: Johannes Liebmann wins gold with a European record over 800 meters
data.translatedDescription: No European has ever been faster over this distance: young star Johannes Liebmann won the 800 meter freestyle in Paris. And that in front of his own teammate Sven Schwarz.

data.title: Berufseinstieg als Segellehrerin: Segelschule statt Olympia
data.description: Eigentlich wollte Laura Pukropski 2032 bei Olympia segeln, dann wurden ihre Fördergelder gestrichen. Um das emotionale Loch zu füllen, übernahm sie eine Segelschule. Den Sport möchte sie zugänglicher machen.
data.translatedTitle: Starting a career as a sailing instructor: sailing school instead of the Olympics
data.translatedDescription: Laura Pukropski actually wanted to sail at the Olympics in 2032, but then her funding was canceled. To fill the emotional hole, she took over a sailing school. She wants to make the sport more accessible.

data.title: Matthias Lilienthal über das »Volksbad«: »Die Duschen sind aktuell nicht funktionsfähig«
data.description: Gerade eröffnete die Berliner Volksbühne ein Schwimmbad, nun muss es schon wieder vorübergehend schließen. Intendant Matthias Lilienthal über die Gründe – und seine Idee, ins »Volksbad« stundenweise nur nicht weiße Menschen zu lassen.
data.translatedTitle: Matthias Lilienthal about the “Volksbad”: “The showers are currently not functioning”
data.translatedDescription: The Berlin Volksbühne just opened a swimming pool, now it has to temporarily close again. Intendant Matthias Lilienthal on the reasons – and his idea of ​​only allowing non-white people into the “Volksbad” for some hours.

data.title: »The End of Oak Street«: Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor im Dino-Chaos
data.description: In »The End of Oak Street« mit Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor wird eine Musterfamilie aus den Achtzigerjahren in die Ära der Dinosaurier versetzt. Gruselig? Ja, aber auch so albern, dass man sich gut unterhalten fühlen kann.
data.translatedTitle: »The End of Oak Street«: Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor im Dino-Chaos
data.translatedDescription: In "The End of Oak Street" with Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor, a model family from the 1980s is transported to the era of dinosaurs. Creepy? Yes, but also so silly that you can feel entertained.

data.title: Travis Kelce spricht erstmals über Hochzeit mit Taylor Swift: »Verrückte Nacht«
data.description: Nein, Fotos der Trauung gibt es immer noch nicht. Aber jetzt hat sich erstmals Taylor Swifts Ehemann geäußert: Travis Kelce beschreibt die »beste Nacht« seines Lebens – und wie er sich mit dem Jawort einen Kindheitstraum erfüllte.
data.translatedTitle: Travis Kelce speaks for the first time about his wedding to Taylor Swift: "Crazy night"
data.translatedDescription: No, there are still no photos of the wedding ceremony. But now Taylor Swift's husband has spoken out for the first time: Travis Kelce describes the "best night" of his life - and how he fulfilled a childhood dream by saying yes.

data.title: Haddad registra candidatura ao governo de SP e declara R$ 861 mil ao TSE
data.description: O ex-ministro Fernando Haddad ( PT ) registrou nesta quarta (12) sua candidatura ao governo de São Paulo e declarou patrimônio de R$ 861,2 mil à Justiça Eleitoral . Leia mais (08/13/2026 - 01h06)
data.translatedTitle: Haddad registers candidacy for the government of SP and declares R$ 861 thousand to the TSE
data.translatedDescription: Former minister Fernando Haddad (PT) registered his candidacy for the government of São Paulo this Wednesday (12) and declared assets of R$ 861.2 thousand to the Electoral Court. Read more (08/13/2026 - 01h06)

data.title: Plano de Flávio Bolsonaro para educação replica o pai em alfabetização e quer pagar aluno para dar reforço
data.description: O plano de governo de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) para educação propõe o método fônico de alfabetização, assim como fez o governo de Jair Bolsonaro (PL), e prevê que estudantes com bom desempenho sejam pagos para dar reforço aos colegas, medida chamada de Programa Acolher. Leia mais (08/13/2026 - 00h03)
data.translatedTitle: Flávio Bolsonaro's plan for education replicates his father's literacy skills and wants to pay students to provide tutoring
data.translatedDescription: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) government's plan for education proposes the phonic method of literacy, as did the government of Jair Bolsonaro (PL), and provides that students who perform well will be paid to support their classmates, a measure called the Acolher Program. Read more (08/13/2026 - 00:03)

data.title: EUA e Colômbia vão realizar ações militares conjuntas em luta antidrogas
data.description: A Colômbia autorizou os Estados Unidos a realizar operações militares conjuntas em "sua luta" contra o narcotráfico , informou nesta quarta-feira (12), no Panamá, o secretário de Defesa americano, Pete Hegseth. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h39)
data.translatedTitle: US and Colombia will carry out joint military actions in the fight against drugs
data.translatedDescription: Colombia authorized the United States to carry out joint military operations in "its fight" against drug trafficking, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth reported this Wednesday (12), in Panama. Read more (08/12/2026 - 11:39 pm)

data.title: Stênio Garcia acusa filhas de questionarem sua sanidade: 'Não admito ser incapacitado'
data.description: O ator Stênio Garcia , 94, publicou um vídeo em seu Instagram nesta quarta-feira (12) acusando as filhas, Cássia Piovesan e Gaya Piovesan, de questionarem sua sanidade mental. Na legenda da publicação, ele mencionou a disputa judicial que trava com elas por um apartamento na Zona Sul do Rio de Janeiro . Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h25)
data.translatedTitle: Stênio Garcia accuses his daughters of questioning his sanity: 'I don't admit being disabled'
data.translatedDescription: Actor Stênio Garcia, 94, published a video on his Instagram this Wednesday (12) accusing his daughters, Cássia Piovesan and Gaya Piovesan, of questioning his mental health. data.title: BC multa Banco Genial em R$ 21,6 milhões e inabilita executivos por falhas
data.description: O Banco Central decidiu nesta quarta-feira (12) multar o Banco Genial em R$ 21,56 milhões por irregularidades em operações de câmbio , comunicação de operações suspeitas ao Coaf e controles internos. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h18)
data.translatedTitle: BC fines Banco Genial R$21.6 million and disqualifies executives for failures
data.translatedDescription: The Central Bank decided this Wednesday (12) to fine Banco Genial R$21.56 million for irregularities in foreign exchange transactions, reporting suspicious transactions to Coaf and internal controls. Read more (08/12/2026 - 11:18 pm)

data.title: Braskem avalia pedir recuperação extrajudicial ainda em agosto, diz agência
data.description: A petroquímica Braskem está em discussões avançadas para um potencial pedido de recuperação extrajudicial, que pode ser protocolado ainda este mês. A medida visa equacionar mais de US$ 10 bilhões em dívidas em suas operações no Brasil, nos Estados Unidos e na Europa, disseram à Reuters nesta quarta-feira (12) duas pessoas familiarizadas com as negociações. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h10)
data.translatedTitle: Braskem is considering requesting extrajudicial recovery in August, says agency
data.translatedDescription: Petrochemical company Braskem is in advanced discussions for a potential request for extrajudicial recovery, which could be filed later this month. The measure aims to settle more than US$10 billion in debt in its operations in Brazil, the United States and Europe, two people familiar with the negotiations told Reuters on Wednesday (12). Read more (08/12/2026 - 11:10 pm)

data.title: Diretor do BC relata à PF ambiente hostil e receio de vazamentos sobre liquidação do Master
data.description: O diretor de Fiscalização do Banco Central , Ailton de Aquino, afirmou à Polícia Federal que havia um ambiente hostil no órgão durante o processo de decisão sobre o futuro do Banco Master , com intensos vazamentos de informações. Por isso, manteve em sigilo a decisão de liquidar a instituição financeira de Daniel Vorcaro , em novembro do ano passado. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h08)
data.translatedTitle: BC Director reports hostile environment to the PF and fear of leaks about Master’s liquidation
data.translatedDescription: The Director of Supervision at the Central Bank, Ailton de Aquino, told the Federal Police that there was a hostile environment in the agency during the decision-making process on the future of Banco Master, with intense leaks of information. Therefore, the decision to liquidate Daniel Vorcaro's financial institution in November last year was kept secret. Read more (08/12/2026 - 11:08 pm)

data.title: Anne Hathaway enfrenta dinossauros em 'O Fim da Rua', filme que chega aos cinemas
data.description: Após enfrentar a crise no jornalismo em "O Diabo Veste Prada 2" e aguardar o retorno de Odisseu em "A Odisseia" , a atriz Anne Hathaway entra mais uma vez em cartaz no cinema. Ela protagoniza "O Fim da Rua", filme que leva dinossauros a uma rua do subúrbio. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h00)
data.translatedTitle: Anne Hathaway faces dinosaurs in 'The End of the Street', film coming to theaters
data.translatedDescription: After facing the crisis in journalism in "The Devil Wears Prada 2" and awaiting the return of Odysseus in "The Odyssey", actress Anne Hathaway enters the cinema once again. She stars in "The End of the Street", a film that takes dinosaurs to a suburban street. Read more (08/12/2026 - 23:00)

data.title: Quilombola de Pernambuco vota em quem conhece: Lula e prefeito de centro-direita
data.description: Estradas de terra cercadas pela vegetação da caatinga serpenteiam as pequenas povoações na zona rural de Salgueiro , cidade de 60 mil habitantes do sertão central de Pernambuco. Uma delas leva até a comunidade quilombola Jurema, onde não há um núcleo urbano e as casas ficam distantes uma da outra. Leia mais (08/12/2026 - 23h00)
data.translatedTitle: Quilombola from Pernambuco votes for who they know: Lula and center-right mayor
